result.narrative:
Larsen & Toubro is a large, financially strong buyer whose underlying payment behaviour remains minor: a single open overdue of INR 18M, 12 days past due, against a INR 350M accepted limit on 90-day terms. Recent corporate news is otherwise strongly positive, including a 14% Q1 net profit rise, multi-billion-dollar AI data centre order wins, and stock rallies, none of which carry credit risk implications.

The Watch band score of 28.4 is driven almost entirely (20.6 of 28.4 points) by a single severity-3 news item: a Karnataka state minister publicly asking officials to blacklist L&T over project delays. The adjudicator agreed with the score's arithmetic but flagged that this story is uncorroborated by any other outlet, has no article body beyond the headline, and reflects a political request rather than a confirmed sanction or blacklisting. Payment history is also thin, with only two data points on record, which the payment_review itself describes as insufficient to establish a trend. The band is therefore plausible but rests on a single headline and limited payment data rather than firm multi-sourced evidence of distress.

The recommended action is to MAINTAIN the current INR 350M limit under policy TCI-WT-2026-0002, as the probability of default (0.1837) remains within appetite (target 0.25) and expected loss is unchanged before and after review. No reduction is warranted given the quality of the underlying evidence.

The score would improve toward Healthy if the blacklisting story is not corroborated or escalated further and/or ages out, combined with the current 12-day overdue resolving promptly as the prior overdue did. It would worsen toward High Risk if the overdue extends materially (to around 38 days past due) or if the regulatory/blacklist matter is confirmed or expands with further adverse coverage.

judgement.bottom_line: Maintain the INR 350M limit; PD is well within appetite, and although the adjudicator agrees the Watch score is arithmetically correct, it flags that the band rests almost entirely on a single, uncorroborated political "blacklist" headline plus thin (two-data-point) payment history rather than confirmed distress.
judgement.payment_note: Only one open overdue is on record - INR 18M, 12 days past due, against a single policy - with a prior overdue settled just 6 days late, but with only two data points the payment_review flags insufficient history to call a clear trend.
judgement.news_note: The dominant news driver is a single-outlet, uncorroborated report of a Karnataka minister asking officials to blacklist L&T over project delays, against a backdrop of otherwise all-positive coverage (strong Q1 profit, large new AI-infrastructure orders, stock rallies).
